newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Mosel raising US$300-400 mln in loans, debt.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Mosel raising US$300-400 mln in loans, debt.

text.p: Taiwan's Mosel Vitelic Inc said on Wednesday it would sign contracts on Thursday for US$200 million in syndicated loans for its $1.7 billion DRAM venture with German electronics giant Siemens AG.
The semiconductor maker also plans to float corporate bonds worth US$100-200 million overseas in December to further finance the expansion, a Mosel executive said.
"We will sign the contract on Thursday for the US$200 million loan for our venture with Siemens," Mosel vice-president William Chen told Reuters by telephone.
"We also plan to raise an additional US$100 to $200 million through issuing corporate bonds abroad in December," Chen said.
The loan would bear an interest rate of LIBOR plus 0.5625 percentage points, Chen said.
"Considering the global semiconductor industry's slowdown since last year, Mosel's success in raising a US$200 million loan with such a low interest rate leaves us feeling quite satisfied," he said.

Fourteen banks, including two foreign banks and 12 local lenders, would join in the loan project, with Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce and International Commercial Bank of China as lead underwriters, Chen said.
Chen said details had yet to be set for the planned December bond issue.
"We haven't finalised the December issue plan, but it's likely to be a corporate bond, not a convertible bond or global depositary receipt," he said.
The loan will be used to finance ProMOS Technologies Inc, a new venture between Mosel and Siemens.

Mosel and Siemens signed contracts in early November to establish the venture to jointly produce advanced dynamic random access memory, or DRAM, chips in Taiwan. Both 64 megabit and 256 megabit DRAMs will be manufactured by the firm.
The venture will be in Taiwan's main high-technology park at Hsinchu, outside Taipei. Mosel will hold 62 percent and Siemens 38 percent.

The partners jointly will invest $1.7 billion in two stages, with the first $1 billion stage expected to start production in mid-1997 and the second $700 million stage to begin production in late 1998, Chen said.
Monthly production capacity will reach 20,000 eight-inch wafers by the end of 1997 and 40,000 wafers by end-1998, Chen said. Mosel is one of the island's leading DRAM makers.
